subject_session: sub-LA11_ses-1 (prototype) + all 15 sessions, 5 mice (LA3, LA8, LA9, LA11, LA12)

headline_stat.name: fraction of units with significant frequency dependence (one-way ANOVA, p<0.01)

justification.dataset: 000986 is the canonical known-good auditory-frequency-tuning dandiset (mouse auditory cortex, Neuropixels, pure tones), exactly the standard choice.
justification.handling: Data are correctly streamed via remfile and trial/unit-aligned, but no explicit unit quality filtering is applied and inclusion is under-justified (all units used).
justification.analysis: Baseline-subtracted evoked rate with a one-way ANOVA across the five frequency groups is an appropriate, correct test of frequency dependence that carries its own null, no circular statistics required.
justification.correctness: Reported fractions reproduce from the committed code, are internally consistent with every figure title, statistically sound, and physically possible.
justification.figures: Figures are clearly labeled with units and sample sizes, example curves are chosen by significance (not slope) and are representative, and the population summary shows the effect convincingly.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate (~75-80%, consistency across sessions noted) and nothing is contradicted by the figures, but no specific limitations are stated and the by-construction nature of the block-diagonal heatmap goes unmentioned, so it sits at generic-caveat level for a genuinely clean result.
justification.verdict: A correct, reproducible, well-presented demonstration of auditory frequency tuning that an expert would accept from a rotation student.
